rows.name: CPUAFFINITY

problems.statement: Unset: the unit and the drop-in give no fallback value.
problems.code_says: The unit expands `${CPUAFFINITY}` inside `ExecStart=/usr/bin/taskset -c ${CPUAFFINITY} ...`. systemd.service(5) says that the `${NAME}` form always gives exactly one argument, so an unset name gives one empty argument. `taskset` cannot parse an empty CPU list, so the instance does not start. The present text does not state this outcome.

problems.statement: A unit comment says platformd writes the first file.
problems.code_says: The sentence reports a comment (house rule 6). The unit itself only shows the two `EnvironmentFile=` lines.

problems.statement: The `tron-host` drop-in starts `rinzler_host` (the rinzler build for CPU inference) the same way.
problems.code_says: The fact holds. The clause defines `rinzler_host` again, which the list "Words used here" already defines (house rule 10). `rinzler` is written without backticks (house rule 4).

cells.Read by: systemd, when it starts the unit `rinzler@.service` (`packaging/systemd/rinzler@.service`, `packaging/tron-host/90-rinzler-host.conf`)
cells.Values and default: A CPU list in the form that `taskset -c` accepts. `taskset` is the Linux command that starts a program on given CPUs. Tron code does not parse the value. Unset: systemd passes an empty CPU list to `taskset`. `taskset` rejects an empty list, and the instance does not start. No file in this repository sets the variable.
cells.Effect: Sets the CPUs that the `rinzler` process may run on when it starts. The unit starts `rinzler` through `/usr/bin/taskset -c <value>`. The `tron-host` drop-in starts `rinzler_host` the same way. `rinzler` binds its application and device threads to its own core sets, for example from `--app-cores` and `--dev-cores`. A thread that `rinzler` does not bind keeps this list. No Tron code reads the list. The unit takes the value from `/etc/rinzler/instance-N.env` or `/opt/positron/user/config.env`.

cells.Values and default: Integer, parsed with `atoi`: the number of hugepages for each NUMA node. Text that is not a number counts as `0`. There is no range check. cells.Effect: Sets the hugepage count of the process. With `--instance`, the count is value x N / 8, rounded down, then x S. rows.name: POS_WEIGHTS_DIR

problems.statement: It applies when a model is loaded with no explicit weights path.
problems.code_says: `resolve_weights()` returns an absolute built-in name as given and reads the variable only for a relative name. `config/models.yaml` holds one `default_weights` entry that is an absolute path, so for that model the variable has no effect.

problems.statement: `--model-path` does not use it.
problems.code_says: Holds. The cell does not draw the result for the packaged service: `packaging/tron-host/README` says that platformd passes `--model-path <weights>:<model>`, and `rinzler` joins that weights field to the fixed root. So the variable has no effect on such an instance.

problems.statement: The path found is made canonical, and the programs read the model files from it.
problems.code_says: Holds (`std::filesystem::canonical`). "made canonical" is an uncommon term, the sentence carries two facts, and the fact only explains the code. The sentence was removed to make room.

cells.Values and default: Path to a directory: the root of the model weights tree. The text is used as given. An empty value counts as unset. Unset: the root is `/opt/positron/weights/huggingface`.
cells.Effect: Sets the root directory under which the built-in weights name of a model, such as `<org>/<model>`, is looked up. It applies when a model is loaded with no explicit weights path and the built-in name is a relative path. A built-in name that is an absolute path is used as given. `--model-path` does not use it. A relative `--model-path` is joined to the fixed root `/opt/positron/weights/huggingface/`. So the variable has no effect on an instance that platformd starts with `--model-path`. A missing directory logs `Weights not found at the source path: <path>`, and the program stops. Check: in `rinzler`, `GET /v1/info` returns the weights path of each model.

rows.name: REPO_ROOT_OVERRIDE

problems.statement: (length) The row has 1,053 characters.
problems.code_says: The statements hold. The row is over the limit of 1,000 characters (house rule 1), and the cell defines "resource map" again (house rule 10). "installed maps" stands for `<program directory>/../config/resource-map.yaml` and `/opt/positron/config/resource-map.yaml`.

cells.Values and default: Path to a directory. Any text that is not empty is used as given. The code does not check that the directory exists. Unset: the repository root is derived from the path of the running program. A program outside a `gen` or `gen-<variant>` build tree has no root.
cells.Effect: Replaces the repository root that the program derives from its own path. The resource map is then searched at `<value>/config/resource-map.yaml`. In a development build of `rinzler` or `runtron`, the default FUSE stats mount directory becomes `<value>/stats`. Search order: `--resource-map`, `resource-map.yaml` in the working directory, this path, installed maps. With Dice, the map comes only from `/opt/positron/config/resource-map.yaml`. `RZ_FUSE_MOUNT_PATH` and `--fuse-mount` override the FUSE path. A development build has `/gen/` in its path. Check: the log line `INIT: Successfully loaded resource map from <path>`.

evidence: h/common/paths.hpp:67 - `getenv("REPO_ROOT_OVERRIDE")`; a value that is not empty is returned as given, with no check of the directory

unresolved: CPUAFFINITY - the row now says that an unset variable stops the instance. The basis is systemd.service(5) (the `${NAME}` form always gives one argument, empty when the name is unset) and the `taskset` parser, which rejects an empty CPU list. It was not run under systemd here. One start of `rinzler@N` on a test host with no `CPUAFFINITY` line in the instance file, followed by `systemctl status rinzler@N`, would settle it.

POS_1GB_PER_NUMA, POS_NR_HUGEPAGES - the rows now say that a count of 0 hugepages stops the process at startup. The basis is the code path (`mmap_file()` with a size of 0 bytes, then `TRON_ASSERT(store != MAP_FAILED)` in src/system/huge.cpp) and mmap(2), which gives EINVAL for a length of 0. It was not run. One start of a hardware test program with `POS_NR_HUGEPAGES=0` on delphi-3b35 would settle it.

POS_HUGEPAGE_PATH - the row now says that an empty value fails startup. The basis is the code path: `scan_hugepage_dir()` opens the parent directory of an empty path, the open fails, the cleanup returns false, and `pos_heap_setup()` returns -1 (src/system/huge.cpp:260, src/system/memory.cpp:149). It was not run. One start of a hardware test program with `POS_HUGEPAGE_PATH=` (empty) would settle it.
